title: Use Snappy output for Dolt garbage collection
body:
Pass archive level 0 through every Beads-owned GC path so new table files use Snappy instead of zstd archives. Existing zstd archive decoding remains unchanged.

Refs #4249.

## Why

Beads does not benefit enough from zstd archive compression to justify its costs. Zstd is the last dependency forcing embedded Dolt builds through CGO, complicating local builds, releases, cross-compilation, and platform support.

Testing also showed that replacing the zstd encoder with klauspost is unsafe: its trained dictionaries provide little benefit over Snappy and can produce archives that existing CGO/libzstd builds reject with a dictionary mismatch.

Dolt already provides a compatible alternative. Archive level `0` writes classic Snappy-compressed table files. Snappy is pure Go, interoperable, and sufficient for typical Beads database sizes. Existing zstd archives remain readable; this change only stops Beads-triggered garbage collection from creating new ones.

This is the safe first step toward pure-Go embedded builds: remove zstd from the write path now, then retain decode-only support for existing zstd archives during the remaining Dolt-side work.
